newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila 1-yr T-bill in demand as rate seen falling.
newsitem.headline: Manila 1-yr T-bill in demand as rate seen falling.

text.p: An anticipated fall in treasury bill rates at the auction on Monday spurred buying in one-year bills in the secondary market, traders said.
The one-year rates give the most attractive yield compared to the other short-term rates, they said.
The high liquidity and low inflation are expected to nudge rates lower at the auction.
"The one year rate could go down as much as 40 to 50 basis points," one trader said.
The benchmarket 91-day T-bill could move down by 20 basis points, another trader said.
A Reuters poll of eight financial institutions gave bids of 11.15/11.25 percent for the one-year bills and offer rates of 11/11.125 percent for the six-month bills.
The interbank call loan rate was unchanged at an average of 14.03125 percent as the Central bank kept its overnight borrowing rate at 14 percent.
Turnover was at 12.66 billion pesos, with 26 lenders and 22 borrowers.
